transcript.text: Morning everyone. Since the monthly cloud-cost review for the image-moderation inference cluster is scheduled for this afternoon, I want to make sure we're aligned before I publish the updated capacity policy. My normal process is to hear from FinOps and ML platform engineering first, so I'd like to get their input on the current state of the cluster. We're running eight GPU nodes in production right now, and the draft policy keeps that as the baseline with a ceiling of ten nodes and a 15-minute scale-up cooldown. Before we finalize, are there any cost or performance concerns we should factor in?

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical performance concern before we finalize this policy. During a load rehearsal for the October 3 image campaign, I measured a sustained requirement for exactly fourteen GPU nodes — well above the proposed ceiling of ten. I also confirmed that the inference queue breaches its latency target unless scale-up begins within exactly five minutes, which is far shorter than the 15-minute scale-up cooldown in the draft policy. I recorded these results in a test notebook but haven't yet attached it to the capacity review document. Given what Casey just shared about the corrected baseline being six nodes, the gap between what we'll have and what October 3 demands is even wider than I initially thought.

Publish the updated capacity policy with baseline of six nodes, ceiling of fourteen nodes, and five-minute scale-up cooldown, incorporating FinOps and ML platform engineering input as per the normal review process.
